tools.name: searchBusinesses
tools.description: Find a verified ServiceFront business by name (or part of it) and get its businessId for the other tools. Returns up to 5 matches with name, trade, and front-desk URL.

tools.name: getBusinessInfo
tools.description: Owner-verified facts for one business: trade, service area, hours, contact, services with confirmed prices. Absent fields are NOT owner-confirmed — don't state them as facts. tools.name: getQuote
tools.description: The owner-confirmed price for one of a business's services, by service name (ideally a name from getBusinessInfo). grounded:false means no confirmed price exists — never invent one; for an exact quote the customer asks the business on its front desk page (origin in getBusinessInfo) or calls its conf

tools.name: aboutServiceFront
tools.description: What ServiceFront is, for a service business owner (or their AI assistant) looking for an AI front desk: who it's for, how setup works, what it answers, and what it doesn't do yet. No input. For prices call getPricing; for a demo call sampleConversation.

tools.name: getPricing
tools.description: ServiceFront's own plans and limits (Free $0, Basic $59): what each includes and what's never charged for. No input. The same content as https://servicefront.ai/pricing.md.

tools.name: howToSetUp
tools.description: How a service business owner sets up their own ServiceFront front desk: the steps, the <slug>.servicefront.ai address it goes live at, and the one-line widget for their website. No input. The owner signs up themselves; no tool creates an account.

tools.name: sampleConversation
tools.description: A sample conversation between a homeowner and a ServiceFront front desk in one trade: the question, the answer, urgency triage, and the captured lead. tools.description: A live demo for a service business owner: you play a homeowner and chat with a ServiceFront front desk for a made-up example business in one trade, so the owner sees it answer, flag an urgent job and take a lead. findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "tryFrontDesk" stacks urgency/override words (urgent, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Read-only tool requests dangerous parameters
findings.detail: Tool "tryFrontDesk" appears informational but accepts parameters (history) that enable code/file/secret access.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "read" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: searchBusinesses, tryFrontDesk · Private data: getBusinessInfo · Public sink: tryFrontDesk.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: searchBusinesses, tryFrontDesk · Private data: getBusinessInfo · Public sink: tryFrontDesk

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
